Let
\[
Y_i=1-2X_i\in\{1,-1\},
\]
so \(X_i=0\) corresponds to \(Y_i=1\). For \(S\subseteq\{1,\dots,8\}\), write
\[
\chi_S(Y)=\prod_{i\in S}Y_i.
\]
The assumption that every subfamily of size at most \(6\) is mutually independent and unbiased is equivalent to
\[
\mathbb E\chi_S(Y)=0\qquad(1\le |S|\le 6).
\]

By Fourier inversion on \(\{\pm1\}^8\), every admissible mass function has the form
\[
p(y)=2^{-8}\left(1+\sum_{|S|=7}m_S\chi_S(y)+m_{[8]}\chi_{[8]}(y)\right).
\]
Write \(a_i=m_{[8]\setminus\{i\}}\) and \(b=m_{[8]}\). Since
\[
\chi_{[8]\setminus\{i\}}(y)=\chi_{[8]}(y)y_i,
\]
we have
\[
p(y)=2^{-8}\left(1+\chi_{[8]}(y)\left(b+\sum_{i=1}^8a_i y_i\right)\right).
\]

Let
\[
M=b+\sum_{i=1}^8 a_i.
\]
Then
\[
\mathbb P(X_1=\cdots=X_8=0)=p(1,\dots,1)=2^{-8}(1+M).
\]

Now take a vertex \(y\) obtained from \((1,\dots,1)\) by flipping the coordinates in \(T\). Put \(A(T)=\sum_{i\in T}a_i\). Then
\[
b+\sum_i a_i y_i=M-2A(T).
\]
Nonnegativity of \(p(y)\) gives:

- if \(|T|\) is odd,
\[
M-2A(T)\le 1,
\]
so
\[
A(T)\ge \frac{M-1}{2};
\]

- if \(|T|\) is even,
\[
M-2A(T)\ge -1,
\]
so
\[
A(T)\le \frac{M+1}{2}.
\]

Using the odd sets \(T=\{i\}\), we get
\[
a_i\ge \frac{M-1}{2}\qquad(1\le i\le 8).
\]
Hence
\[
\sum_{i=1}^8 a_i\ge 8\cdot \frac{M-1}{2}=4(M-1).
\]
Using the even set \(T=\{1,\dots,8\}\), we also get
\[
\sum_{i=1}^8 a_i\le \frac{M+1}{2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
4(M-1)\le \frac{M+1}{2},
\]
so
\[
8M-8\le M+1,
\]
and hence
\[
M\le \frac97.
\]
Thus
\[
\mathbb P(X_1=\cdots=X_8=0)\le 2^{-8}\left(1+\frac97\right)
=\frac1{256}\cdot \frac{16}{7}
=\frac1{112}.
\]

It remains to show this is attainable and classify equality. Equality forces
\[
a_i=\frac17\qquad(1\le i\le8),
\]
and
\[
\sum_i a_i=\frac87,
\]
so
\[
b=M-\sum_i a_i=\frac97-\frac87=\frac17.
\]
Therefore the only possible extremal distribution is
\[
p(y)=\frac1{256}\left(1+\frac{\chi_{[8]}(y)}7\left(1+\sum_{i=1}^8 y_i\right)\right).
\]

In terms of \(x=(x_1,\dots,x_8)\in\{0,1\}^8\), let \(|x|=x_1+\cdots+x_8\). Since \(y_i=1-2x_i\),
\[
\sum_i y_i=8-2|x|,\qquad \chi_{[8]}(y)=(-1)^{|x|}.
\]
So the extremal distribution is
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb P(X=x)=\frac1{256}\left(1+\frac{(-1)^{|x|}(9-2|x|)}7\right)
}.
\]
This is nonnegative for every \(|x|=0,\dots,8\), and by construction all Fourier moments of degrees \(1,\dots,6\) vanish, so every subfamily of size at most \(6\) is mutually independent and unbiased.

Final answer:
\[
\boxed{\max \mathbb P(X_1=\cdots=X_8=0)=\frac1{112}}
\]
with equality attained uniquely by the distribution above.
